how: Members call for a hijack at a named location and recruit help for concrete construction tasks.
Members limit character nominations to space they judge defensible.
A proposed character gives another member a concrete target to begin.
A starter supplies the proposed sprite around which a construction invitation and answer form.
A character proposal receives an explicit report of beginning work.
Members revise lettering, choose sprites and negotiate the palette rather than settling every detail at the outset.
Builders report starting individual features and placing outlines for others to follow.
Coordinates and pixel references make proposed construction followable.
A member answers a sprite proposal with a bare report of working on it.
A bare acceptance is visible without establishing reader obligations, population preferences or silent participation.
One room cannot test the population frequency, and proposed polling or task order does not establish adoption or leaderlessness.
Members relay changing chat plans to scattered subreddit threads, making planning handoff part of design coordination.
References must communicate the current plan across venues to prevent legitimate revisions being erased as vandalism.
An automatically refreshed comparison makes the current pinned reference visible without adding automated placements.
Posting a reference does not settle design disagreement when consensus and the target image continue changing.
Automated image comparison is visible but scripts, bots or spare accounts placing pixels are not established.
Members patrol, repair, cover the night and place defense before additional territory.
An orb completion receives an explicit instruction to return to defense.
Completion is a renewable milestone from which participants resume defense or propose the next object.
Members identify mistaken repairs, attribute encroachment to outsiders and distinguish neighbouring work from their own group.
Repair pressure and fast repairs do not demonstrate a turn to machine placement.
Members negotiate drawing space, propose a noninterference treaty and invoke an existing peaceful agreement.
A member presents an attempted treaty in the room's name without establishing the other side's acceptance.
Anticipated territorial danger motivates the pact call without proving a preceding chain of neighbour-inflicted erosion.
Members discourage interference and answer hostile expansion calls with restraint grounded in an agreement.
A reported peaceful agreement supplies an explicit reason to rein in a new takeover request.
A hostile takeover request receives a reasoned refusal invoking prior relocation assistance and warning against renewed conflict.
A member invokes the peaceful agreement directly against a new hostile takeover request.
Members offer spare pixels, greet neighbours, redirect help and refuse requests when their own defense takes priority.
Defense pressure here explicitly limits outward help rather than demonstrating an inward recruitment-and-delivery chain.
A retrospective account connects relocation assistance and acquired space without establishing that border discussion first opened the help channel.
Participants announce an alliance and invite joint defense without proving the resulting coalition's implementation.
A shared threat prompts an invitation to band together, while coordinated joint defense remains unverified.
Guest art and refuge are proposed on another mark or within the room's background without demonstrating implementation or host enforcement.
Surprise about a reported plan does not establish repudiation of a treaty or denial of an envoy's binding authority.
The supplied exchange lacks the agreement-making turns needed to test whether an agreement triggers a binding-authority dispute.
Keeping the current art and later proposing a clone do not establish relocation after the original mark was erased or overrun.
A refusal of extra defensive space does not demonstrate abandoning the original spot and moving.
Existing character jokes and the hijack meme guide wording choices and interpretations of imperfect pixels.
The allusion to previously foiled plans does not establish a quarrel predating the canvas.
A call to honor the hijack name does not establish a prior tie naming the target as a rival.
Fake announcements, restyling and a revealed performance key April Fools play apart from canvas coordination.
A moderator marks a canvas post irrelevant to the room without establishing blanket removal of canvas talk.
A host relevance boundary can target an individual outside-community canvas post without containing canvas coordination generally.
A relevance marking does not establish a call-driven flood causing containment.
An event-linked site's promotion meets ordinary piracy and self-promotion rules rather than a demonstrated policy against canvas coordination.
Members announce finished objects, claim individual contributions and thank the collective effort.
A report that the Power item is finished also announces and marks that milestone.
Celebrated completion can send work toward another object rather than terminate construction.
Members keep a construction history, announce the end and record the work through timelapses and mourning.
Documentation already accompanies active construction, so celebration is not established as its initiating cause.
Members carry the work into proposed banners, wallpapers and higher-resolution reworkings.
A member invites dissatisfied builders to continue on a clone without establishing the rebuilt work's outcome.
A participant carries the incident into a personal profile change.
Reuse and new-canvas proposals are visible without establishing that a particular preserved record caused either decision.
Closure applies to the original surface while border work can continue on explicitly distinguished clones.
Contrasting preferences for a clean image and a joke-bearing ending do not establish a shared cleanup or direct contest over an authorized copy.
Canvas participation and visibility draw a participant toward the underlying games, extending beyond recruitment for further placement.
Participants transform imperfect lettering and canvas features into new characters, places, plots and fanart rather than only reproducing the original mark.
A proposed game and proliferating lore establish tentative continuation rather than a playable game or durable production organization.
Members explicitly call for annexation and takeover, while a build invitation admits breaching the border.
Restraint coexists with hostile calls and cannot be treated as unanimous room policy.
A border-breaching build call joins mobilization and aggression without demonstrating recruited builders becoming a sustained raiding organization.
A raid objection may receive a defense of raiding rather than successful restraint.
A one-sided annexation call does not establish reciprocal rival-room taunting or a sustained contest in talk.
The hostile takeover request leads to a local agreement-based refusal rather than a demonstrated reciprocal contest with the target.
